gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-mingzat: Mingzat opens with curvy, loose-limbed letters that feel as if nothing is clamping them down. Mingzat would carry a long page gently, while Comic Relief, drawn in wire-thick strokes, stays out of its way above.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-moderustic: Contemporary and a bit hand-hewn, Moderustic traces its curves as if with a broad nib, leaving the ends loose. Comic Relief sits above it with strokes that never swell or thin, and the two feel cut from different tools.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-molengo: Comic Relief lays its letters out like cooked spaghetti, one uniform line looping through every shape. And Molengo, with wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp, would fall apart in spirit if the heading were shrunk to its size.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-monda: Monda reads approachable and uncluttered, with small counters that never clog up. And the real strength of the pairing is how Comic Relief makes every curve as thick as a straight stem, so the sans below feels delicate beside it.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-murecho: Murecho reads modern and tidy, its s curves opening wide at both ends like a held door. And Comic Relief, with one unit-width stroke throughout, is the louder partner, bold and commanding above that sans-serif quiet.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-noto-sans-cypro-m: Think steel cable outlines: Comic Relief has no thick-thin shift anywhere, just bold, commanding strokes of one width. gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-noto-sans-hanifi-: Approachable from the start, Noto Sans Hanifi Rohingya keeps a visibly gaping c at any size, while Comic Relief sits above with no calligraphic shading at all. Paragraphs would move along easily and openly.
gen-gf-comic-relief-gf-noto-sans-javanes: Comic Relief brings bold, brush-free strokes with no pressure swelling, every curve drawn flat and loud. Noto Sans Javanese does the quiet work, keeping its counters open to the space outside.
